scene_description: A small tiled bedroom with a foreground bed, open shelving and a narrow cabinet against the back wall, two floor lamps, an open doorway, and a white furniture panel at right.
initial_target_observations: The initial reconstruction shows a dark doorway with only a narrow pale vertical strip at its right edge; the broad open door leaf visible in the reference is absent from view.
candidate_target_observations: The candidate shows a pale, paneled open door leaf extending into the room and partly covering the dark doorway. It is much narrower in the image than the reference leaf and does not extend as far toward the foreground or overlap the bed area in the same way.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The door reads as a thin upright leaf with an inset panel, although its apparent angle and size differ substantially from the reference. The shelf, cabinet, lamps and bed remain recognizable, but their projected positions and proportions differ. The candidate's right-hand white panel is less prominent and differently shaped than in the reference. Image evidence cannot establish actual hinge attachment, contact or collisions.
new_visible_defects: No clear new defect is established beyond the remaining mismatch in door silhouette and its foreground occlusion.
other_changes: The candidate framing shifts the bed and back-wall furniture rightward relative to the initial image. Both reconstructions use comparatively uniform gray flooring and soft neutral lighting, unlike the reference's mottled floor, warmer illuminated wall, stronger shadows and visible wood grain. The reference cabinet has glazed upper doors, whereas the candidate's upper doors appear opaque.

evidence.description: Large pale wood-paneled door leaf projects into the room and overlaps the foreground scene.
Dark doorway and narrow light edge, without a comparably visible broad door leaf.
A visible pale paneled leaf now covers part of the doorway, though it is much smaller in the frame than the reference door.
Glazed cabinet doors, warm lamp glow and mottled floor provide material and lighting detail.
The narrow cabinet and rear lamp are present, with opaque-looking doors and more uniform lighting.

uncertainty: The door's visible appearance is closer to the reference, but differences in framing and viewpoint affect apparent size and occlusion. A single RGB view does not establish hidden geometry, physical contact, collisions or longer-term capability.
